sections.title: Review of Systems and System Thinking, Software 🖥️

content.subtitle: What is a System? ⚙️
content.description: A system is an interrelated set of business procedures or components working together within one business unit to achieve a purpose. It's an organized collection of parts (subsystems) highly integrated to accomplish an overall goal.

content.subtitle: What is Systems Thinking? 🧠
content.description: Systems thinking is the ability to see organizations and information systems as systems. It's a holistic way to investigate factors and interactions contributing to an outcome. It operates on the philosophy that all things are connected, essential for problem-solving.

items.definition: Breaking a system into smaller subsystems or components.
Dividing a system into chunks or modules of relatively uniform size.
Subsystems should be as independent as possible (Loose Coupling).
The extent to which a subsystem performs a single function (High Cohesiveness).

content.subtitle: Software 💾
content.description: Software is a product within information systems. Software engineering is the process involved in its development.

content.subtitle: Goals of System/Software Development 🎯
content.description: Problem-solving and supporting business processes. Involves Users, Managers, Analysts, Designers, Programmers, and Consultants.

content.subtitle: Inherent Nature of Software Complexity 🕸️
content.description: Industrial-strength software exhibits rich behavior, maintains large data with concurrent access, or controls real-world entities. These systems have long lifespans and many dependent users.

content.subtitle: Characteristics of Complex Systems 🌌
content.description: Intensely difficult for a single developer to comprehend entirely. Complexity is an essential property of large software systems.

items.definition: Real-world problems involve changing requirements and competing stakeholder needs.

items.term: Difficulty of managing the development process 👥
items.definition: Involves team management and coordination.
Software is highly flexible and labor-intensive, lacking strict standards.

items.term: Problems of characterizing the behavior of discrete systems ⚠️
items.definition: Uncontrollable inter-state changes can corrupt systems if not carefully crafted.
Systems are composed of interrelated subsystems, forming hierarchies.
Choice of primitive components is subjective, depending on abstraction level.
Hierarchic systems are nearly decomposable, with stronger linkages within components.
Composed of few subsystem types in various combinations.
Evolve from simple systems that worked.

content.subtitle: Solution for Software Complexity 🛠️
content.description: Decomposition is the solution to manage complexity.

items.definition: Top-down, structured design focusing on processes and event ordering.
Decomposes based on key abstractions, focusing on objects and data.

content.subtitle: Software Crisis 🚨
content.description: Arises from communication difficulties and complexity management. Failure occurs when software stops delivering expected results.

items.definition: Easy to design, maintain, and reuse parts.
Easy to learn, efficient, solves problems at acceptable cost.
Sells more, pleases customers, costs less to develop.
Solves problems at acceptable cost.

content.subtitle: Structured Paradigm 📜
content.description: Developed in the 1970s/1980s. Models process and data separately. Suitable for small-sized software.

items.definition: Top-down, data-centered, functional decomposition.
Improve quality, reduce failure risk, establish concrete requirements.

content.subtitle: Object Oriented Paradigm 🧬
content.description: Systems are collections of interacting objects with data and behavior. Uses bottom-up approach.

items.definition: Object-centered, emphasizes reuse and design patterns.

sections.title: The Potential Benefits and Drawbacks of Structured System Analysis and Design 📊

items.definition: Easier for users/programmers to understand.
Makes good use of graphical tools.
A mature technique.
Easy to understand and implement.
Not enough user-analyst interaction.
Hard to decide when to stop decomposing.
Cumbersome with large-scale systems.
Misses encapsulation and object orientation.

sections.title: The Potential Benefits and Drawbacks of Object Orientation System Analysis and Design 🧬

items.definition: Reduces code volume, improves quality.
Better suited for large, complex systems.
Encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism.
Better modeling of complex relationships.
Steep for those unfamiliar with OO.
Hard to understand high-level functions.
Difficult to understand data-process relationships.

content.subtitle: What is Object Technology (OT)? 🛠️
content.description: Umbrella term for OO programming, databases, and design methodologies. Objects contain data and logic.

items.definition: Combine data and logic to represent real-world entities.
Properties representing object state (e.g., color, size).
Blueprint specifying structure, behavior, and inheritance.
Task performed by an object, hiding implementation details.
Constructing an object from its class blueprint.
Classes can be reused to build reliable systems.
Messages sent to objects to perform tasks.
Hides internal data and procedures, exposing minimal interface.
New classes extend existing ones, inheriting properties.
Methods apply to general classes with specific responses.

sections.title: The Object Orientation Software Process Models ⚙️

content.subtitle: Software Development Process 📋
content.description: Uses Methodologies, Techniques, and Tools to create systems.

items.definition: Step-by-step approaches to develop products.
Processes to ensure thorough work.
Programs to support techniques.

content.subtitle: Modeling 🖼️
content.description: Abstract representation of real or imaginary entities.

content.subtitle: Object-Oriented Analysis and Design (OOAD) 🧬
content.description: Views systems as interacting objects. Determines requirements and designs solutions.

items.definition: Identifies requirements and builds real-world object models.
Refines analysis model, includes system and object design.
Translates design into code and tests for errors.

content.subtitle: Unified Modeling Language (UML) 📊
content.description: Notation system for OO analysis, design, and deployment.

items.definition: Diagrams visualize components and interactions.
Provides precise models for activities.
Models map to OO languages.
Tracks development activities.

content.subtitle: Object-Oriented Pattern 🧬
content.description: Abstraction of small class groupings useful in OO development.
